title: Ansarallah Advances, Israel Murders, Trump Withdraws, and Why Iran Still Controls the Strait: The War Brief
author: Murtaza Hussain
content:
On this week's episode of the War Brief, hosts Sarmad Jawad and Murtaza
Hussain break down the most critical military and foreign policy developments
across the Middle East and Eastern Europe over the past week.

In Yemen, Ansarallah, also known as the Houthis, continue their rapid advances
across western Yemen, moving to encircle the city of Taiz and firming up their
control control over the vital Bab al-Mandab Strait. As Saudi Arabia
reportedly plans a major military offensive against the group with the support
of regional countries, Ansar Allah is establishing facts on the ground in
their battle to control Yemen.

In Gaza, the Israeli military has continued to carry out strikes killing
Palestinian civilians in Gaza--including deadly strikes targeting journalists
and members of Gaza's small Christian community. According to most recent
figures, Gaza's Health Ministry has recorded at least 1,431 Palestinians
killed and 5,026 wounded since the October 2025 ceasefire.

In Europe, Moscow has issued a direct warning to NATO, threatening the use of
its full military arsenal--including nuclear weapons--if Western operations
isolate the militarized exclave of Kaliningrad.

Meanwhile in Iraq, U.S. allies in Iraq feel betrayed by Trump's withdrawal of
forces from the country, even as many ordinary Iraqis celebrate the
withdrawal.

Despite claims from Donald Trump, Tehran firmly maintains control over the
Strait of Hormuz, striking eight oil tankers in just five days. Iran is
preparing contingency plans for an escalated conflict, including likely
targeting of naval and aerial support bases like those on the Indian Ocean
island Diego Garcia.
